searchText: > git index I meant that more as an inspiration, than something to necessarily be used verbatim - they've done a good job though, in general, since git is.. fast :) > block trees agree that it would be nice - we'd have to sacrifice some of the simplicity though > finalized slot in the header we lose append-only at that point which makes it more vulnerable to corruption, in general - it would also require moving the non-finalized portion around to compact it, so that offsets remain O(1) the biggest issue I see with storing stuff in this format is that you actually don't store the blocks that resulted in the previous blocks being finalized - that's.. ugly, when loading! > finalized blocks in this format on disk y - it's pretty much ideal for this use case - compact, fast etc > we lose append-only at that point which makes it more vulnerable to corruption, in general - it would also require moving the non-finalized portion around to compact it, so that offsets remain O(1) Mmm, true. Perhaps it would make sense as two separate files (finalized + non-finalized) I don't think we'd use this internally (I like to let the database do _some_ of the work of managing consistency 😅 ), but we may use the general idea of flattening out our finalized blocks so that they're contiguous on disk > flattening this is pretty much what we intend to do - ie flatten the blocks out of the db into a finalized file - there are indeed some consistency concerns here - a starting point is to get it done as import/export because it would be really useful to have, even with weak subjectivity states since there's interest, I'll ship that doc over to the spec repo as a PR, so we can have a more constructive discussion

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content:
> git index
I meant that more as an inspiration, than something to necessarily be used verbatim - they've done a good job though, in general, since git is.. fast :)
> block trees
agree that it would be nice - we'd have to sacrifice some of the simplicity though
>  finalized slot in the header
we lose append-only at that point which makes it more vulnerable to corruption, in general - it would also require moving the non-finalized portion around to compact it, so that offsets remain O(1)

the biggest issue I see with storing stuff in this format is that you actually don't store the blocks that resulted in the previous blocks being finalized - that's.. ugly, when loading!

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content:
>  finalized blocks in this format on disk 
y - it's pretty much ideal for this use case - compact, fast etc

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content:
> we lose append-only at that point which makes it more vulnerable to corruption, in general - it would also require moving the non-finalized portion around to compact it, so that offsets remain O(1)
Mmm, true. Perhaps it would make sense as two separate files (finalized + non-finalized)

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: I don't think we'd use this internally (I like to let the database do _some_ of the work of managing consistency 😅 ), but we may use the general idea of flattening out our finalized blocks so that they're contiguous on disk

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content:
> flattening
this is pretty much what we intend to do - ie flatten the blocks out of the db into a finalized file - there are indeed some consistency concerns here - a starting point is to get it done as import/export because it would be really useful to have, even with weak subjectivity states

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: since there's interest, I'll ship that doc over to the spec repo as a PR, so we can have a more constructive discussion
